title: Man shot by cop was known to police
article: A machete-wielding young man shot dead by a police officer had prior contact with police, although he did not have a criminal record, says a spokesman for the suburban Port Moody department.
Const. Brian Soles said Tuesday that Keyvan Tabesh,18, was running at the officer with the machete when he was struck down.
Soles said statements from the two witnesses at the scene support the police version of events.
Tabesh, of Burnaby, B.C., was shot a number of times by a plainclothes officer early Monday morning.
Police are continuing their investigation to confirm that the officer properly identified himself before shots were fired.
Police said the teen was prohibited from driving, but was behind the wheel of his car with two male friends before the shooting.
Earlier Monday, Tabesh attacked another car with a machete, after bumping it with his car.
While the two women occupants, both in their 20s, were inside, Tabesh "went nuts on the car," Soles said. "He didn't know them."
As police were taking the women's statements, Tabesh passed by in his car. Another officer was radioed to respond and pursued the car to a dead-end street.
Tabesh and one youth got out and approached the officer, who fired at both men.
Tabesh died, while the other man is expected to be released from hospital after non-life-threatening injuries.
"Somebody made a mistake that night," said Soles. "It was them."
He said there were several ways out at the end of the cul-de- sac.
"These people did not have their backs to the wall. If they wanted to get away from police they had ample avenues available to them."
Police say Tabesh came to Canada from the Middle East two years ago and that he dropped out of high school last year.
An autopsy was performed Tuesday, but results were not immediately available.
It will be up to B.C.'s chief coroner to decide whether to hold an inquest into the death.
The officer who was involved in the incident is on sick leave, pending an internal investigation.
